title: Resumable tenant feedback throttle and graceful fast-fail for hosted API during escalations
creator: Ava Rodriguez
description:
Summary:
We saw multiple customer escalations over the past two weeks where aggressive client retries + long-lived streaming connections produced tenant-local connection pool starvation and KV-cache churn, which triggered sustained 5xx waves and timeouts for otherwise healthy tenants. This ticket implements a server-side, resumable tenant feedback throttle paired with a graceful fast-fail path and client signaling header to reduce cascading failures during escalations.

Observed failure pattern (repro / telemetry):
- Tenant burst generates large number of short-lived and streaming requests with high token churn.
- Edge proxy connection pool becomes saturated by long-lived streams; new requests queue and time out upstream (504/524).
- SDKs detect timeouts and immediately retry without backoff; retries amplify load and cause KV-cache thrash/evictions on runtime nodes.
- Runtime slowpaths (large attention windows / cold KV rebuilds) create long-tail latencies and intermittent 5xx.
- Affected tenants then observe sustained degraded throughput and persistent customer escalations.

Root cause analysis (current hypothesis):
1) Admission control at the edge lacks tenant-aware credits; tenants can consume an unbounded fraction of accept slots under burst.
2) SDKs currently implement optimistic retries with short jitter that worsen bursts.
3) KV-cache eviction heuristics are not reacting to tenant-local access hotspots quickly enough, causing repeated cold-path penalties.
4) There is no explicit server-side retry advisory to guide SDK behavior during partial degradations.

Proposed changes (strategy):
- Server-side tenant credit bucket (resumable): allocate a small real-time credit pool per tenant at the edge. Credits consumed per request type (stream vs non-stream) and reclaimed on graceful shutdown. When credits are exhausted, return a fast-fail with advisory headers rather than allowing request queuing.
- Retry advisory header: add X-Redwood-Retry-Advice with values (none|short|backoff|fastfail) and X-Redwood-Retry-After to indicate recommended wait. SDKs will treat fastfail as terminal for current attempt and surface clear guidance to users/clients.
- Streaming admission soft-limit: enforce a per-tenant concurrent stream cap lower than connection pool size; streams will be accepted until soft-limit then accepted as resumable or rejected fast with resume token hint where applicable.
- KV-cache compaction tuning: add tenant-aware compaction frequency and prefetch heuristics for high churn tenants to reduce repeated cold rebuilds on the runtime.
- Proxy keepalive and connection admission tuning: reduce keepalive TTL for idle streaming sockets on overloaded hosts and implement a jittered connection draining policy to avoid synchronized reconnect storms.

Trade-offs considered:
- Fast-fail reduces throughput for some requests but prevents full-service degradation. We prefer predictable failures with advisory guidance over opaque retries that amplify incidents.
- Tenant credit buckets add memory/state at the edge; small per-tenant state is required but scale targets accepted (bounded map + eviction).
- Changing SDK guidance requires coordinated rollout; we will ship server-side headers first and then backfill SDKs incrementally.

Implementation plan and milestones:
1) Design doc and simulation (done): Confluence doc linked above. Micro-simulation shows 35-60% reduction in 5xx spike amplitude for synthetic tenant bursts.
2) Edge implementation (week 1): credit-bucket admission control, headers, fast-fail path. Unit + integration tests. PR: https://github.com/redwood/inference/pull/6124.
3) Runtime changes (week 1-2): KV-cache compaction heuristics, prefetch on warmup, and soft limit enforcement. PR: https://github.com/redwood/inference/pull/6130.
4) Staged rollout (week 2): Canary to non-prod regions then 10% production traffic in region-us-east-1, observe SLOs for 48h. Metrics: per-tenant 5xx-rate, p95/p99 latency, connection pool occupancy, KV-cache hit ratio, queued requests.
5) SDK advisory rollout (week 3): release SDK patch that reads X-Redwood-Retry-Advice and implements backoff/resume behavior. Provide fallback: if no header, behavior unchanged to preserve compatibility.
6) Customer comms and support runbook: prepare clear messaging for escalated customers explaining fast-fail semantics, and a temporary customer override to increase their credits in case of purchased reserved capacity.

Testing and validation:
- Unit tests for credit accounting and fast-fail semantics.
- Integration test simulating 200 tenants with random burst patterns using loadgen harness.
- Chaos test: induce KV eviction on a subset of runtimes to validate graceful degradation and advisory header propagation.
- Observability: add new Grafana panels, alerts for >10% of requests receiving "fastfail" header, and end-to-end trace correlation for advisory header lifecycle.

Rollback and mitigation plan:
- Feature is behind feature flag. Rollback by disabling flag at edge control plane.
- If rollout correlates with increased customer-reported errors, we will temporarily increase per-tenant credits for paying customers and enable a global emergency policy to accept all requests for a limited window (while additional mitigations applied).

Open questions / follow-ups:
- What should the default credit sizing be for free-tier vs paid customers? (PM input required).
- How to represent resume tokens for streaming in a client-agnostic way without leaking internal state? (security and product review).
- Should we expose a per-tenant dashboard for credits consumed to the Console? (UX/PM).

Links to artifacts:
- Design: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Resumable+Tenant+Throttle+Design
- Edge PR: https://github.com/redwood/inference/pull/6124
- Runtime PR: https://github.com/redwood/inference/pull/6130
- Load test dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/hosted-api/tenant-5xx?orgId=1

Acceptance criteria (done > all):
- Edge returns advisory headers reliably under load and fast-fail prevents queue growth > 5s for new requests.
- SDK patch respects advisory header and reduces retry amplification in integration tests.
- Production canary results show reduction in per-tenant 5xx amplitude by >=30% without regression in p50 latency for other tenants.

Notes from triage: multiple customers (support case IDs attached to Slack thread) reported repeated attempts ended up with duplicated application-side events; idempotency guidance will be included in SDK release notes.
